title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 252
paragraphs: They are religious excessively, beyond all other men, and with regard to this they have the following customs. They drink from cups of bronze and rinse them out every day — not some only do this, but all. They wear garments of linen always newly washed, and of this they make a special point. They circumcise themselves for the sake of cleanliness, preferring to be clean rather than comely. The priests shave themselves all over the body every other day, so that no lice or any other foul thing may come upon them when they minister to the gods. The priests wear garments of linen only and sandals of papyrus, and no other garment may they take, nor other sandals. They wash themselves in cold water twice by day and twice again by night; and they perform other religious services of almost infinite number. They enjoy no few good things also, for they do not consume or spend anything of their own substance; there is sacred bread baked for them, and each of them has a great quantity of beef and goose-flesh coming in to him every day, and wine of grapes is given to them too — but it is not permitted them to taste of fish. The Egyptians do not sow beans at all in their land, and what grow of themselves they neither eat raw nor boil for food; indeed the priests cannot bear even to look upon them, thinking them an unclean kind of pulse. There is not one priest only for each of the gods but many, and of these one is chief priest; and whenever a priest dies his son is appointed to his place.
